discovery: Ab initio molecular dynamics (the Car-Parrinello method)

nominees.name: Michele Parrinello
nominees.affiliation: Italian Institute of Technology (IIT), Genoa, Italy

subfield: Condensed matter physics - computational and first-principles materials theory
motivation: In 1985 Car and Parrinello combined density-functional electronic structure with classical molecular dynamics in a single unified Lagrangian. For the first time, atoms could be moved by forces computed on the fly from quantum mechanics, at finite temperature and without empirical potentials. This turned first-principles theory from a tool for static, idealised crystals into a predictive physics of real matter: liquids, amorphous solids, surfaces, phase transitions, and materials under extreme pressure and temperature, including planetary interiors, dense hydrogen and water. Their approach, and Parrinello's later work on simulating phase transitions and rare events, led directly to the computational methods now used throughout condensed matter physics. Those methods underpin today's knowledge-based materials design and the machine-learned interatomic potentials built from them. Prediction followed by experimental confirmation has become routine because of this discovery. It is a foundational advance in physics of the highest order.
